_comment: 议题投票数据。candidates=未辩候选(供投票)，debated=已辩(链到辩论)。投票免 GitHub 登录，存于自建后端(Cloudflare Worker + D1，见 ~/Desktop/cissy0802.github.io/engage-backend/)：每候选一个 poll，key='topic:'+id，choice up/down，净票=👍−👎。votes 字段由 routine 每次跑 `python3 refresh_votes.py`(读后端 /votes-net) 回写；页面 ideas.js 也会实时拉取覆盖显示。观众自提议题在评论 page='thinker-open-questions'，各候选下讨论 page='topic:'+id——routine 读这些把好提案提炼成新 candidates。新候选加进 candidates 即可。

candidates.q: 该不该吃肉？动物有没有值得我们尊重的道德地位？
candidates.q_en: Should we eat meat? Do animals have a moral standing we're bound to respect?
candidates.note: 辛格说，能感受痛苦就该被纳入道德考量，『物种歧视』和种族歧视一样站不住脚；可儒家讲『亲亲而仁民、仁民而爱物』的差等之爱，庄子又说万物齐一。一个你每天在做、却很少严肃质疑的选择。
candidates.note_en: Singer argues that whatever can suffer deserves moral consideration, and 'speciesism' is as indefensible as racism; yet Confucianism teaches a graded love radiating outward, and Zhuangzi sees all things as one. A choice we make daily but rarely question.

candidates.q: 民主一定是最好的制度吗？
candidates.q_en: Is democracy necessarily the best system of government?
candidates.note: 柏拉图把民主比作让乘客投票指挥航船、终将触礁，主张哲人王；托克维尔警惕『多数人的暴政』；法家信赏必罚的强力，熊彼特把民主降格为『精英竞争选票』。一个几乎不容置疑的『神圣价值』，值得被认真盘问一次。
candidates.note_en: Plato likened democracy to passengers voting to steer a ship onto the rocks, and argued for philosopher-kings; Tocqueville warned of the 'tyranny of the majority'; Legalism trusts strict reward and punishment, and Schumpeter reduced democracy to 'elites competing for votes.' A near-unquestionable 'sacred value' worth interrogating.

candidates.q: 该不该信命？算命、八字、星座为何长盛不衰
candidates.q_en: Should you believe in fate? Why do fortune-telling and astrology endure
candidates.note: 是迷信，还是另一种自我认知？　求签、八字、星座至今风靡：是廉价的心理安慰、放弃能动性的借口，还是一面帮人看清自己的镜子？孔子『不知命无以为君子』与『敬鬼神而远之』的张力、斯多葛的命运之爱(amor fati)、荣格的共时性、萨特『人是自己选择的总和』正面交锋。
candidates.note_en: superstition, or another way of knowing yourself? Divination, bazi and astrology still thrive: cheap psychological comfort, an excuse to surrender agency, or a mirror that helps people see themselves? The tension in Confucius between 'without knowing fate one cannot be a gentleman' and 'respect the spirits but keep them at a distance,' the Stoic amor fati, Jung's synchronicity, and Sartre's 'man is the sum of his choices' collide.

candidates.q: 死刑该废除吗？国家有没有权力剥夺一个人的生命？
candidates.q_en: Should the death penalty be abolished? Does the state have the right to take a life?
candidates.note: 康德的报应论——杀人者偿命才是对其人格的尊重；贝卡里亚开创废死——国家无权杀人、威慑存疑、冤案不可逆。正义、威慑、报应、人的尊严，以及『以命偿命』到底是正义还是另一桩杀戮，正面相撞。
candidates.note_en: Kant's retributivism — a life for a life is the only way to respect the murderer as a person; Beccaria, founder of abolitionism — the state has no right to kill, deterrence is doubtful, and a wrongful execution cannot be undone. Justice, deterrence, retribution, human dignity, and whether 'a life for a life' is justice or just another killing collide head-on.

candidates.q: 「工作与生活的平衡」是能达成的状态，还是一句自我安慰？
candidates.q_en: Is work–life balance an achievable state or a comforting myth — is there balance at all, or only tradeoffs?
candidates.note: 到底有没有平衡，还是只有取舍？　短期里时间精力是零和，『平衡』常被当成能一劳永逸的稳态，达不到反增愧疚；可它也能指长周期的季节轮换、或工作即生活的一部分而非对立面，而『只有取舍』又容易把 996 这类制度问题私人化。Naval『没有平衡，只有优先级』对上罗素《悠闲颂》、塞内卡《论生命之短暂》、凯恩斯的闲暇预言，与纽波特的深度／边界。另一面是『该把多少自己押进这份工作』：敬业内卷与『安静离职』之争、把工作当事业还是当一桩生意——韦伯的新教伦理与铁笼、马克思的异化、庄子的『无用之用』都在这条线上。 另一条并进来的线是『闲』：不事生产的『无用』时光到底有没有价值，又该怎么和懒区分。 另一条并进来的线是『把自己当成一项资产来经营』：『投资自己』『提升个人价值』『打造个人品牌』这套语言把人讲成一件必须持续增值的东西，休息一天都像在贬值——当一个人开始用回报率衡量友情、休假与孩子，人力资本究竟是解放，还是最精致的一层异化？
candidates.note_en: In the short run time and energy are zero-sum, and 'balance' is often treated as a steady state to be reached once and for all — falling short only breeds guilt; yet 'balance' can also mean seasons rotating over a long life, or work as part of life rather than its opposite, while 'only tradeoffs' risks privatizing structural problems like the 996 grind. Naval's 'no balance, only priorities' against Russell's In Praise of Idleness, Seneca's On the Shortness of Life, Keynes's leisure prophecy, and Newport's depth/boundaries. The other face of it is how much of yourself to stake on the job at all: devotion and overwork against 'quiet quitting', treating work as a calling or as a transaction — Weber's Protestant ethic and iron cage, Marx on alienation and Zhuangzi's 'usefulness of the useless' all sit on this line. A further strand folded in: does unproductive, 'useless' time have value of its own, and how is it told apart from idleness? A further line folds in here: running yourself as an asset. 'Invest in yourself', 'raise your personal value', 'build your personal brand' — the vocabulary casts a person as something that must keep appreciating, so that a day of rest feels like depreciation. Once someone starts measuring friendships, holidays and children by rate of return, is human capital a liberation or the most refined layer of alienation?

candidates.q: 精神痛苦，是该吃药修复的『脑病』，还是对处境的正常/有意义反应？
candidates.q_en: Is mental suffering a 'brain disease' to be fixed with medication, or a normal, meaningful response to one's situation — is medicating all pain relief, or silencing?
candidates.note: 把痛苦一律药物化，是解脱还是消音？　抑郁到底是『血清素失衡』要靠 SSRI 修的脑病，还是身体对糟糕处境（或存在困境）发出的正常信号？萨波尔斯基的生物化学决定论对上弗兰克尔的意义疗法（痛苦可以有意义，别急着消除）、萨斯的『精神病的神话』（问题是生活的，不是脑子的病）、福柯的『什么被定义成病』，再加哈里斯谈冥想与意识。接得住 value-of-suffering，但切的是医学化 vs 意义这条新轴。也含更大的一问：我们是不是把太多正常的人生状态（悲伤、走神、内向、衰老）『医学化』成了病——过度诊断与 DSM 的不断扩张，究竟是识别了以前被忽视的痛苦，还是诊断标签与药物市场的合谋？也含更根本的一问：痛苦本身有没有价值，一个彻底没有苦难的世界值不值得要。　也含：悲伤、走神、内向、衰老被『医学化』成病，过度诊断与 DSM 扩张是进步还是合谋；也含更根本的一问：痛苦本身有没有价值，一个彻底没有苦难的世界值不值得要 也含『情绪究竟长在哪里』这一相邻角度：詹姆斯说先有身体反应才有情绪，达马西奥的躯体标记把感受落到内脏，而斯多葛与认知派说情绪本是判断——离开心跳、肠胃与荷尔蒙，还会不会有真正的喜怒哀乐？答案不同，处方也就不同。 也含一个相邻角度：恐惧与痛苦首先是一套预警系统，误报值得磨掉，漏报却要命——把所有不适一律当成待修复的信号，会不会连真实的警报也一起磨钝？以及长期在高压与道德冲突中工作的人（医生、社工、举报者）的耗竭与『道德损伤』，该记在病历上，还是记在处境的账上。 也含一条落到诊室的相邻角度：当第一人称的自述与第三人称的测量冲突时（检查全部正常、人却确实在疼），谁有最终发言权？把自述当证据而非判决、把测量当材料而非判决，这条中间规矩能不能操作化。
candidates.note_en: Is depression a 'serotonin imbalance' brain disease to be fixed by SSRIs, or a normal signal the body sends about a bad situation (or an existential bind)? Sapolsky's biochemical determinism meets Frankl's logotherapy (suffering can hold meaning — don't rush to erase it), Szasz's 'myth of mental illness' (problems are of living, not of the brain), Foucault on what gets defined as illness, plus Harris on meditation and consciousness. It picks up value-of-suffering but cuts a new axis: medicalization vs meaning. It also carries the larger question of whether too many ordinary states of life — grief, distraction, introversion, ageing — have been medicalized into illnesses, and whether ever-expanding diagnostic manuals recognize suffering that was previously ignored or serve the market that treats it. It also carries the deeper question of whether suffering has any value at all, and whether a world entirely free of it would be worth having. It also absorbs the adjacent question of where an emotion actually lives: James held that the bodily reaction comes first and the feeling after, Damasio's somatic markers place feeling in the viscera, while the Stoics and the cognitive tradition treat an emotion as a judgement. Without the heartbeat, the gut and the hormones, would there be any joy or grief at all? Different answers imply different prescriptions. It also carries an adjacent angle: fear and pain are first of all an early-warning system, whose false alarms are worth grinding down and whose misses are the dangerous ones — so does treating every discomfort as a signal to be repaired eventually blunt the real alarms too? And where should the exhaustion and 'moral injury' of people who work for years under pressure and moral conflict — doctors, social workers, whistleblowers — be recorded: on a medical chart, or against the situation? It also carries an adjacent angle that lands in the consulting room: when a first-person report and a third-person measurement conflict — every test normal and the person genuinely in pain — who has the last word? Can the middle rule be made operational: a report is evidence rather than a verdict, a measurement material for a verdict rather than the verdict itself?

candidates.q: 为了公共健康，国家能限制个人自由到什么程度？
candidates.q_en: For the sake of public health, how far may the state limit individual freedom (mandatory vaccines, lockdowns, sugar taxes, smoking bans) — and where does that power come from in the first place?
candidates.note: （强制疫苗、封控、糖税、禁烟；同一把尺该不该量向广告、无限下拉、成瘾式设计这类制造欲望与注意力的产业；也含更根本的一问：国家的这份权力从何而来、有没有正当的边界）　2020 年代最撕裂的真问题：密尔的『伤害原则』止于何处？福柯的『生命权力』——现代国家正是靠管理『人口的健康』来行使治理，对上伯林的消极自由、洛克的个人权利，与功利主义/公共卫生的集体福祉正面交锋。个人自主 vs 集体安全，边界到底划在哪。同一把尺该不该量向制造欲望与注意力的产业：广告、无限下拉、成瘾式设计——如果糖税与禁烟成立，凭什么不管它们？还是说管制欲望本身就越界了？　更根本的一层：这份权力究竟从何而来——社会契约、天命，还是法家式的强力？来源与边界是政治哲学最古老的争点，也决定了上面每一条禁令该由谁点头。
candidates.note_en: The most divisive real question of the 2020s: where does Mill's 'harm principle' stop? Foucault's 'biopower' — the modern state governs precisely by managing 'the health of the population' — meets Berlin's negative liberty and Locke's individual rights, colliding head-on with the utilitarian/public-health case for collective welfare. Personal autonomy vs collective safety: where exactly is the line? The same yardstick can be turned on the industries that manufacture desire and harvest attention — advertising, infinite scroll, addictive design. If sugar taxes and smoking bans are legitimate, why not these? Or is regulating desire itself a step too far? A deeper layer: where does that power come from at all — a social contract, the Mandate of Heaven, or Legalist force? Source and limit are political philosophy's oldest quarrel, and they decide who is entitled to sign off on any of the prohibitions above.

candidates.q: 有没有放之四海皆准的美德，还是善恶本就因文化、时代而异？
candidates.q_en: Are there universal virtues, or are good and evil relative to culture and era
candidates.note: 我们该向谁的道德看齐？　同一件事，一处的美德可能是另一处的恶习：孝顺、忠诚、勇敢的内容随文化而变，甚至彼此冲突。道德是可跨文明求真的『一套』，还是各有各的约定？休谟的『是与应当』、尼采的价值重估、孔子的礼、人类学的文化相对论各执一端——若无共同标尺，宽容与批判又各以何为据？
candidates.note_en: whose morality should we measure by? The same act can be a virtue in one place and a vice in another: the content of filial duty, loyalty and courage shifts with culture and can even conflict. Is morality a single truth pursuable across civilisations, or a set of local conventions? Hume's is–ought gap, Nietzsche's revaluation of values, Confucian ritual and anthropological cultural relativism pull in different directions — and without a shared measure, on what do tolerance and critique each rest?

candidates.q: 外貌在多大程度上是一种『资本』？
candidates.q_en: To what extent are looks a form of 'capital'
candidates.note: 该承认颜值红利、好好经营，还是该抵制这种不公？　招聘、相亲、镜头前，好看的人确有实打实的溢价（『颜值红利』）。这是该像投资技能一样经营的社会资本，还是一种该被抵制的、给人贴标签的不公？经济学（贝克尔、哈基姆的『情色资本』）对上正义论与女性主义。
candidates.note_en: should we acknowledge and cultivate the beauty premium, or resist it as unjust? In hiring, dating, and on camera, the good-looking enjoy a real premium ('pretty privilege'). Is this social capital to be cultivated like a skill, or an unjust, labeling advantage to be resisted? Economics (Becker, Hakim's 'erotic capital') meets theories of justice and feminism.

candidates.q: 当权力把『裁员』改叫『优化』，我们还能守住自己的判断吗？
candidates.q_en: When power renames 'layoffs' as 'optimization,' can we still hold on to our own judgment?
candidates.note: 委婉语、行话与口号如何不禁止你开口就替你预设结论。　委婉语、行话与政治口号如何在不禁止你开口的情况下替你预设结论；乔姆斯基的『制造同意』，普通人识破话术、还原朴素事实的自保之道。　也含法律/金融/学术『黑话』——是必要的精确，还是把人挡在门外的墙？清晰表达是不是一种被低估的正义（鲁迅白话之问）。　同一种操作的另一面：把一个选择重述成『规律』——宇宙法则、优胜劣汰、人性本贪、市场自会决定——责任就从选择者身上转移给了世界。检验的办法或许是看引用之后紧接着要做的那个动作。　也含道歉的通货膨胀：当企业公告、明星声明与政客致辞都学会了那套完整话术——说清做了什么、承认规矩、承诺改进、给出补偿——每一步都能被排练、外包、由公关审过。当动作本身不再稀缺，受损的一方还剩什么判据可用：赔偿的金额、规则被重新执行的证据，还是那个人此后真的付出了代价？
candidates.note_en: How euphemism, jargon and slogans preset your conclusions without ever forbidding you to speak; Chomsky's 'manufacturing consent,' and how an ordinary person sees through the spin and restores the plain fact. It also covers legal/financial/academic jargon — necessary precision, or a wall that keeps people out? Is plain speech an underrated form of justice (Lu Xun's vernacular question)? The same manoeuvre has another face: restate a choice as a 'law' — of the cosmos, of survival of the fittest, of human greed, of the market — and responsibility passes from the chooser to the world. The test may be to watch the action that follows immediately after the citation. It also covers the inflation of apology: now that corporate statements, celebrity notes and political addresses have all learnt the full script — state the act, acknowledge the rule, promise the change, offer redress — every step can be rehearsed, outsourced and cleared by a communications team. When the gestures are no longer scarce, what criteria are left to the injured party: the size of the restitution, the evidence that the rule is enforced again, or whether the person actually bore a cost afterwards?

candidates.q: 凡事都追求『最优／高效』，是不是正在系统性地掏空我们的韧性？
candidates.q_en: By chasing 'optimal' and 'efficient' in everything, are we systematically hollowing out our resilience?
candidates.note: 冗余、备份、『暂时没用的多样』，该不该刻意保留？　从供应链到个人生活，我们把冗余当浪费一路砍掉，换来风平浪静时的高效；可韧性恰恰藏在那些『用不上』的备份、多样与慢里。效率与韧性能不能兼得，还是终究得取舍？该在哪里刻意留白？也含面对小概率大灾难时的决策规则：科学给出的是区间、政策却只能落一个数字，该按最可能值还是按承受得起的最坏值来定——预防原则是审慎，还是让人瘫痪。　另含一条相邻角度：城市规划与算法在同一个方向上追求『无摩擦』——导航给点对点最短路径、外卖免掉去店里那一趟、推荐流滤掉不合口味的，物理世界的『撞见』与信息世界的『不期而遇』被同时剪掉；生活越来越像一次次搜索：带着目的去、拿到就走。摩擦、绕路与浪费掉的时间，能不能被有意识地重新装回去？ 也含国与国这一层：分工越细、比较优势越极致，断供与卡脖子的代价也越高——『把生产搬回本国』究竟是买保险，还是用效率换来的一层昂贵冗余？
candidates.note_en: Should redundancy, backups, and 'currently useless' variety be deliberately kept? From supply chains to personal life, we cut redundancy as waste and buy efficiency for calm times; yet resilience lives precisely in the backups, variety and slack that look 'useless.' Can efficiency and resilience coexist, or must we trade them off — and where should we deliberately leave slack? It also carries the decision rule for low-probability, high-damage events: science hands over a range while policy can only settle on one number, so should it be set at the most likely value or at the worst one you could survive — is the precautionary principle prudence, or paralysis? One adjacent angle folded in: urban planning and algorithms both chase the frictionless — navigation supplies the shortest point-to-point route, delivery removes the trip to the shop, recommendation feeds filter out whatever is not to taste, and so bumping into someone physically and stumbling on something unexpected online are cut away together. Life comes to resemble a series of searches: arrive with a purpose, collect, leave. Can friction, detours and wasted time be deliberately built back in? It also covers the international layer: the finer the division of labour and the more extreme the comparative advantage, the costlier a cut-off or a chokepoint becomes — is reshoring production buying insurance, or paying for an expensive layer of redundancy with efficiency?

candidates.q: 该给关系做减法吗？
candidates.q_en: Should you prune your relationships?
candidates.note: 断掉消耗你的人与义务，是必要的自我保护，还是把自己越活越窄？　对物的断舍离我们有一堆判据，对人的断舍离几乎没有门槛：难缠的亲戚、要长期投入的友谊、照顾谁的义务、无聊却重要的场合——这一刀省下的时间最多，也最不可逆。一边是边界、止损、远离有毒关系；一边是耐受度下降、把关系当成本核算、以及成本被转嫁给那些还愿意留下来的人。判据该是什么：伤害的性质、可修复性、你在其中的位置？另含两个相邻角度：①关系有自然衰减率，长期不接触就自动往外掉一层——一旦知道这条规律，『保持联系』就从情谊变成要排进日程的维护工作，那还算不算感情？②在退不出去的家族、村落与熟人职场里，人不缺联结，缺的是不解释就能消失两小时的权利：不同社会的短板，究竟是进不去还是退不出？　还有一个相邻角度：躲开算不算一种正当的解决方式。人人都说时间会冲淡，可淡掉的也许不是记忆本身，而是遇到触发线索的机会——若真如此，搬家、换工作、退出一个群就该被当成正经的手段，而不是逃避；何况降低接触频率往往是当事人唯一能单方面执行的办法。回避，究竟是没面对，还是最有效的面对？
candidates.note_en: Is cutting off the people and duties that drain you necessary self-protection, or a life quietly narrowing itself? We have plenty of criteria for decluttering objects and almost none for decluttering people: the difficult relative, the friendship that needs sustained investment, the duty to care for someone, the boring but consequential occasion. That cut frees the most time and reverses the least. On one side: boundaries, cutting losses, leaving toxic relationships. On the other: a shrinking tolerance for friction, relationships accounted for as costs, and those costs transferred to whoever is still willing to stay. What should the criteria be — the nature of the harm, whether it can be repaired, your own position within it? Two adjacent angles also belong here: (1) ties decay on their own — go long enough without contact and one drops a layer — and once you know the rate, 'keeping in touch' becomes an upkeep task on a calendar rather than affection, which raises the question of whether it is still affection; (2) inside a clan, a village or a workplace where everyone knows everyone, people do not lack connection but the right to vanish for two hours without explaining, so the real deficit may be the inability to get out rather than to get in. One adjacent angle: whether avoidance counts as a legitimate solution. Everyone says time dulls things, but what fades may not be the memory itself so much as the frequency of meeting its cues — and if so, moving house, changing jobs and leaving a group chat deserve to be treated as real measures rather than evasion, especially since lowering contact is often the only step a person can take unilaterally. Is avoidance a failure to face something, or the most effective way of facing it?

candidates.q: 一个人能在多大程度上既拒绝共同体的要求，又指望共同体的托底？
candidates.q_en: How far can a person decline what a community asks of them while still counting on its safety net
candidates.note: 自立的人对社会还欠什么，社会又欠他什么？　独来独往、不参加、不搭理，被越来越多人当作正当的活法；可现实里替独行者兜底的仍是家人、邻居、公共医保与养老金。于是问题不再是『合群好不好』，而是权利与义务对不对称：能不能只要退出的自由、不要参与的义务？反过来，社会有没有资格用『你不贡献』去削减对一个人的照顾？照护、急救、失业救济这些托底，究竟是无条件的人的资格，还是共同体成员身份的对价？ 也含：有能力的人纷纷买下私立学校、私人医疗与私家车而退出公共服务之后，剩下的人还托不托得住。　一个具体的入口：你存下的钱里，有多少是自己的选择，有多少是医疗、养老、失业的公共缺口开给你的账单？后者本就没有上限，所以怎么存都不够。
candidates.note_en: what does the self-reliant still owe society, and what does society still owe them? Keeping to yourself — not joining, not answering — is increasingly treated as a legitimate way to live; yet in practice the backstop for the loner is still family, neighbours, public health insurance and pensions. The question is then no longer whether sociability is good but whether rights and duties are symmetrical: can one claim the freedom to withdraw without the duty to take part? And conversely, is a society entitled to cut what it gives a person on the grounds that they contribute nothing? Are care, emergency treatment and unemployment support unconditional entitlements of persons, or the consideration paid for membership in a community? Also: once those who can afford it withdraw into private schools, private medicine and private cars, does the floor still hold for everyone left. A concrete way in: of the money you have put aside, how much is your own choice and how much is the bill handed to you by the gaps in healthcare, pensions and unemployment cover? The second column has no ceiling by design, which is why no amount is ever enough.

candidates.q: 一个人的优点和缺点，是不是同一个特点的两面？
candidates.q_en: Are a person's strengths and flaws two faces of the same trait
candidates.note: 若真如此，改掉缺点会不会连优点一起改掉？　高尽责＝可靠 ⇄ 完美主义僵化；高共情＝温暖能读人 ⇄ 界限模糊被淹没；高开放＝创造好奇 ⇄ 不聚焦烂尾——同一套底层机制必然同时产出两种结果（人格特质本身价值中立，进化上叫拮抗多效性）。但要打三个折扣：很多缺点（残忍、失信、自欺）根本没有对应优点，同源论易沦为免责声明；更常见的其实是剂量或场合错了（亚里士多德中庸），不是必然代价；评价还随环境翻转。检验：去掉那个缺点，优点还在吗？亚里士多德（中庸·德性可调）× 荣格（阴影须整合）× 尼采（别阉割自己的强力）× 达尔文/萨波尔斯基（拮抗多效性与气质的生物底）对上 孔子/王阳明（克己·变化气质）与『这是自我合理化』的诘问方。
candidates.note_en: and if so, does fixing the flaw also destroy the strength? High conscientiousness means reliable yet rigidly perfectionist; high empathy means warm and perceptive yet boundary-less and flooded; high openness means creative and curious yet unfocused and prone to abandoning things — one underlying mechanism necessarily yields both results (personality traits are value-neutral; evolution calls this antagonistic pleiotropy). But three discounts apply: many flaws (cruelty, dishonesty, self-deception) have no corresponding strength at all, so the same-root claim easily becomes a blanket excuse; more often the real issue is wrong dosage or wrong setting (Aristotle's mean), not a necessary price; and the valuation flips with environment. The test: remove the flaw — is the strength still there? Aristotle (the mean; virtue is adjustable) × Jung (the shadow must be integrated) × Nietzsche (don't geld your own strength) × Darwin/Sapolsky (antagonistic pleiotropy and the biology of temperament) against Confucius/Wang Yangming (self-mastery, transforming one's disposition) and a challenger who calls it rationalization.

candidates.q: 我们记得的过去，有多少是重新编造的？
candidates.q_en: How much of the past we remember was rebuilt on the spot
candidates.note: 记忆若不可靠，『我是谁』还立得住吗？（同一问题的另一面：靠冥想、致幻剂、极限体验换来的『顿悟』，是真知还是大脑的一场花样——脑子给我们的经验，凭什么当证据）　记忆不是录像带，而是每次回想都被重写一遍的重建。洛夫特斯只用一句提示就能植入从未发生的童年往事，目击证词因此送错过人；而我们的身份、亲密关系与恩怨账本，全架在这份不可靠的记录上。若记忆总是按当下的需要改写过去，『忠于事实的自我』还成立吗？遗忘又该算缺陷还是恩赐——尼采说没有遗忘就无法生活，博尔赫斯笔下过目不忘的富内斯反而丧失了思考。奥古斯丁的『记忆之宫』、普鲁斯特的非自愿记忆、佛教的种子熏习，对上洛夫特斯与沙克特的实验，再加一个现实追问：当聊天记录、照片流与 AI 摘要替我们保存一切，外置的记忆会矫正我们，还是取代我们？ 同一问题的另一面：靠冥想、致幻剂、极限体验换来的『顿悟』，是真知还是大脑的一场花样——脑子交给我们的经验，凭什么当证据？ 　由此还牵出两问：一是后见之明——你现在知道那条路不通，恰恰因为你走过了，再拿这份知识回头审当年的自己，等于用今天的答案去考一个还没上过课的人；二是若每次取回都在重写，那么叙事疗法、写信、复盘这类『与过去和解』的做法，在机制上是不是就是在合法地改写记忆，而当那件事还牵着别人时，谁有权改写共同的那一段？ 也含一个更硬的追问：意识从不以复数出现，你从未经验过两份、只知道有一份——那么一个『我』究竟靠什么划出边界？换掉记忆算不算换了人？
candidates.note_en: and if memory is unreliable, does 'who I am' still stand? Memory is not videotape but a reconstruction rewritten on every recall. Loftus could implant a childhood event that never happened with a single suggestion, and eyewitness testimony has sent the wrong people to prison; yet our identity, our intimacies and our ledgers of grievance all rest on this unreliable record. If memory always edits the past to suit the present, does 'a self faithful to the facts' survive? And is forgetting a defect or a gift — Nietzsche held that without forgetting one cannot live, while Borges's Funes, who forgot nothing, lost the ability to think. Augustine's palace of memory, Proust's involuntary recollection and the Buddhist perfuming of seeds meet the experiments of Loftus and Schacter, plus a practical question: now that chat logs, photo streams and AI summaries keep everything for us, will externalised memory correct us or replace us? The same question from the other side: is the 'insight' won through meditation, psychedelics or extreme experience real knowledge, or a trick of the brain — on what grounds does experience handed to us by the brain count as evidence? Two further questions follow. First, hindsight: you know that road leads nowhere precisely because you walked it, and turning that knowledge back on your earlier self is examining someone on a course they had not yet taken. Second, if every retrieval rewrites, then narrative therapy, letter-writing and the post-mortem — the standard ways of 'making peace with the past' — are mechanically a licensed rewriting of memory; and when other people are attached to the event, who has the right to rewrite the part that is shared? It also carries a harder question: consciousness never occurs in the plural — you have never experienced two of it and know only of one — so what actually draws the boundary around a single 'I', and would replacing the memories replace the person?

candidates.q: 仪式还有用吗？
candidates.q_en: Do rituals still do anything?
candidates.note: 在一个不太信神的时代，礼仪的正当性从哪里来？涂尔干说仪式制造的是共同体而非神迹，人类学看它标记身份的转换，心理学看它给不确定的情绪一个形状与终点。可代价是真实：走过场的婚礼、被指标化的葬礼、公司的团建。哪些仪式该保留、该改造、该废掉——判据是什么？　也含一个来自『忠诚该不该被考验』的角度：婚礼誓词、入职宣誓、公开许诺，都是当众进行、双方知情的检验——它们也许根本不在测量已有的承诺，而是在生产承诺：让人当着众人付出一笔收不回的代价，从此难以反悔。若仪式的功能是制造不可撤销，那么在一个什么都能撤回的时代，它该怎么重做？
candidates.note_en: Weddings, funerals, anniversaries, opening ceremonies: empty forms and social obligation, or scaffolding the mind cannot do without? In an age that largely does not believe in gods, where does the legitimacy of ritual come from? Durkheim held that rites manufacture community rather than miracles; anthropology reads them as markers of transitions in status; psychology sees them giving formless emotion a shape and an end. The cost is authenticity: the wedding gone through by rote, the funeral reduced to a checklist, the corporate away-day. Which rites should be kept, which reworked, which abolished — and by what test? It also carries an angle from the debate on testing loyalty: wedding vows, oaths of office and promises made in public are all examinations conducted before witnesses with both parties fully informed — and they may not measure an existing commitment at all but manufacture one, by extracting a cost in public that cannot be recovered, after which going back becomes hard. If the function of ritual is to make something irrevocable, how should it be rebuilt in an age where almost everything can be undone?

candidates.q: 该不该把家底留给孩子？
candidates.q_en: Should you leave your wealth to your children?
candidates.note: 把房子、存款、人脉传下去是天经地义的自由，还是机会平等最大的那个漏洞？留多少算爱，留多少就成了替他决定一生？　制度层面几乎人人反对世袭特权，回到自家餐桌，却几乎人人想把房子、存款与人脉留给孩子。继承是家庭最自然的延续，也是不平等代际复制最主要的通道：一代人的运气经由它变成下一代的起点。留多少算爱、留到多少就成了替他决定一生？巴菲特那句『多到能做任何事，少到不能什么都不做』给了一条经验线；遗产税、赠与、学区房与人脉引荐则是同一件事的不同马甲。还有一问：把钱留给孩子与捐出去，哪一个才对得起自己那份运气？　还有一层：多数家庭的钱不是一个人的账户，而是几个人之间从没写下来的合约——父母的养老预期、给孩子留多少、伴侣两套金钱观在同一张卡上打架。这场谈判该由谁先开口？
candidates.note_en: Is passing on the house, the savings and the contacts an obvious liberty, or the largest loophole in equal opportunity? At the level of policy almost everyone opposes inherited privilege; back at the family table almost everyone wants to leave the house, the savings and the contacts to their children. Inheritance is the most natural continuation of a family and also the main channel through which inequality reproduces itself across generations — one person's luck becomes the next generation's starting line. How much counts as love, and at what point does it decide a life on someone's behalf? Buffett's rule of thumb — enough to do anything, not enough to do nothing — draws one line; estate tax, lifetime gifts, catchment-area housing and a word in the right ear are the same act in different clothes. And a further question: does leaving it to your children or giving it away do more justice to the luck you were handed? And a further layer: in most households money is not one person's account but an unwritten contract among several — a parent's expectations for old age, how much to leave a child, two financial temperaments fighting over one card. Who is supposed to open that negotiation?

candidates.q: 谁有权拿别人的人生下注？
candidates.q_en: Who is entitled to bet other people's lives?
candidates.note: 创始人、将领、政客付出的『不可撤销的代价』，押上的常常不是自己的东西　我们习惯把『为一个判断付出昂贵而不可撤销的代价』当成它出于远见而非豪赌的证据。可押上去的常常是员工的十年、股东的钱、士兵的命、一整条供应链的生计——事前有没有办法区分『自己下注』与『替别人下注』？如果一个人要求他人承担的风险远大于自己承担的，他展示的还算不算勇敢？再往下还有一问：被押上去的人凭什么算同意——一纸雇佣、一张选票、一道军令，够不够；押错之后又该怎么赔。亚里士多德的勇敢与鲁莽之辨、塔勒布的切肤之痛、马基雅维利、韦伯的责任伦理都能入场。　也含：当一个人永久失去自主能力，该按什么替他做决定——照他先前表达过的意愿，还是照旁人判断的最佳利益？以及父母替孩子承担风险时，可恢复的损失与一旦触到就回不来的损失，事前该怎么分辨。 也含：该不该给地球动手术——平流层遮阳、海洋施铁这类气候工程，由少数人决定、风险却落在所有人与后代身上，谁有资格按下这个开关。　同一道题的家庭版本：二十几岁的人要不要出走、要不要换城市，看起来是个人选择，实际由家庭这个单位承担——父母何时需要人在身边、家里有没有第二个人顶得上、汇款要不要继续。一个人的探索，该由谁一起签字？
candidates.note_en: the irreversible price paid by a founder, a general or a politician is usually not their own We habitually treat paying an expensive, irreversible price for a judgement as proof that it came from foresight rather than bravado. Yet what gets staked is usually ten years of employees' lives, shareholders' money, soldiers' lives, an entire supply chain's livelihood — so is there any way, before the result arrives, to tell betting your own stake from betting someone else's? If a person asks others to carry far more risk than they carry themselves, is what they display still courage? A further question follows: on what basis are the people staked said to have consented — does an employment contract, a vote or a military order suffice — and what is owed to them when the bet fails? Aristotle on courage versus recklessness, Taleb on skin in the game, Machiavelli, and Weber's ethic of responsibility all belong here. Also included: when someone permanently loses the capacity to decide, by what standard should others decide for them — their previously expressed wishes, or another's judgement of their best interests? And when parents take risks on a child's behalf, how does one tell in advance a recoverable loss from one there is no coming back from? Also: whether to operate on the planet — stratospheric sunshades, ocean iron fertilization and the like, decided by a few while the risk falls on everyone and on those not yet born. Who is entitled to press that switch? The household version of the same question: whether someone in their twenties leaves, or moves cities, looks like a personal choice yet is borne by the family as a unit — when parents will need somebody present, whether a second person at home can step in, whether the remittance continues. Who else should be signing off on one person's exploration?

candidates.q: 我们该为上一代做过的事负责吗？
candidates.q_en: Are we answerable for what earlier generations did?
candidates.note: 道歉、赔偿、纪念碑与教科书——一个人没做过的事，凭什么由他来还？　雅斯贝尔斯把罪分成刑事、政治、道德与形而上四层，说只有第一层能上法庭；阿伦特反对『集体罪责』，认为人人有罪等于无人有罪；可现实里国家在道歉、企业在赔偿、后代仍在继承那份好处。继承了红利算不算继承了债？幸存者的愧疚、家族的旧账与国家的历史责任，是同一件事的不同尺度吗？　另一端是既不能罚、也不能恕的那一类：加害者已经去世、系统性失职无处追索、父母永远不会承认——两种终止方式同时失效时，人还剩下什么可做？纪念、书写、把这件事讲给下一代听，算不算第三种终止？
candidates.note_en: Apologies, reparations, monuments and textbooks — why should anyone repay what they never did? Jaspers divided guilt into criminal, political, moral and metaphysical, and held that only the first belongs in a court; Arendt rejected collective guilt on the grounds that where everyone is guilty no one is. Yet states apologise, companies pay reparations, and descendants go on inheriting the benefit. Does inheriting the dividend mean inheriting the debt? And are survivor's guilt, a family's old accounts and a nation's historical responsibility the same thing at different scales? At the other end are the wrongs that can be neither punished nor forgiven: the offender already dead, a systemic failure with no one to sue, a parent who will never concede. When both ways of halting a thing have failed, what is left to do — and do memorial, writing and telling the next generation amount to a third way of making it stop?

candidates.q: 有没有人类永远想不明白的事？
candidates.q_en: Are there things humans can never understand?
candidates.note: 狗永远学不会微积分；人的认知硬件会不会也有天花板？内嗅皮层的网格细胞按平面铺格子，我们对空间的表征天生是三维的——谈更高维时并不是在想象，只是在符号上滑行，再把顺畅误当成理解。那么数学符号、仪器与 AI 算不算『外接的感官』，能把天花板推到多高；又该怎么分辨『暂时不懂』与『原则上不可懂』？ 也含『理解是不是必需品』这一相邻角度：量子力学的测量问题悬置百年，量子计算机照样开跑；模型越来越准也越来越黑箱。当工程上『闭嘴计算』就够用，解释还剩什么位置——科学还需不需要哲学来追问它自己在说什么？
candidates.note_en: A dog will never learn calculus; does human cognitive hardware have a ceiling of its own? Grid cells in the entorhinal cortex tile a plane and our representation of space is natively three-dimensional — above three dimensions we are not imagining anything, only skating along a symbolic surface and mistaking the smoothness for comprehension. Do mathematical notation, instruments and AI count as prosthetic sense organs, and how far can they push the ceiling back? And how would we tell 'not understood yet' from 'unintelligible in principle'? It also carries the adjacent question of whether understanding is required at all: the measurement problem in quantum mechanics has been suspended for a century while quantum computers run anyway, and models grow both more accurate and more opaque. When 'shut up and calculate' is engineering-sufficient, what work is left for explanation — and does science still need philosophy to ask what it is saying?

candidates.q: 不用钱来分，就更公平吗？
candidates.q_en: Is an allocation made without money any fairer?
candidates.note: 排队、抽签、按需要、按资历、按人脉、按行政审批——把稀缺的好东西移出市场之后，这些方式各自会滋生什么样的腐蚀？排队奖励有闲的人，认定需要的权力立刻成为新的稀缺资源，靠关系分配则把价码压进不透明也无法拒绝的人情。器官名单、学区、公立医院的加号、稀缺岗位的推荐，谁在这些规则下赢，谁被悄悄挡在门外？ 同一问题在组织内部的版本是背书与推荐：当机会靠同事的作证与人脉分配，怎样的可核查标准才能把健康的同侪见证与小圈子的互相抬轿分开？
candidates.note_en: Queues, lotteries, need, seniority, connections, administrative approval — once a scarce good is taken off the market, what corruption does each of these breed? Queues reward those with time to spare; the power to certify need instantly becomes the new scarce resource; allocation through connections buries the price in favours that are neither transparent nor refusable. Organ lists, school catchments, the extra slot at a public hospital, the referral into a scarce job: who wins under these rules, and who is quietly kept out? The same question inside an organisation takes the form of endorsement and referral: when opportunity is allocated by colleagues vouching for one another, what checkable standard separates honest peer testimony from a clique boosting its own?

candidates.q: 该坚持，还是该及时止损？
candidates.q_en: Persist, or cut your losses?
candidates.note: 一件看不到回报的事，撑下去是毅力还是沉没成本？　照顾一个不会好转的病人、守着一份没有反馈的研究、写一本可能没人读的书——需要三年的耐力和需要三秒的胆量几乎不共用同一套机制：后者靠一次到位的动作，前者靠意义结构与能让你明天还起得来的日常。同一种坚持，事后既可能被叫作毅力，也可能被叫作不肯认输。有没有事前就能立的止损线？把退出条件写下来，是先认输，还是让投入变得付得起？达克沃思的 grit 对上卡尼曼的沉没成本谬误，弗兰克尔的意义对上『及时放弃也是一种能力』。
candidates.note_en: When something shows no return, is staying with it grit or sunk cost? Caring for a patient who will not recover, staying with research that gives no feedback, finishing a book that may go unread — three years of endurance and three seconds of nerve barely share a mechanism: the second runs on one well-aimed action, the first on a structure of meaning and a routine that gets you up tomorrow. The same persistence is called tenacity or refusal to admit defeat depending on how it ends. Can a stop-loss be set in advance, and does writing down your exit conditions concede the fight or make the commitment affordable? Duckworth on grit meets Kahneman on the sunk-cost fallacy, and Frankl on meaning meets the claim that quitting in time is itself a skill.

candidates.q: 钱、婚姻、国界，是真实的东西吗？
candidates.q_en: Are money, marriage and borders real things?
candidates.note: 它们不长在原子里，也不长在某一个人的念头里——靠许多人相互承认而持续存在，大家同时不认便真的消失，纸币变回纸。这类『共建的实在』既非唯物亦非唯心，却最能左右普通人的命运：房价、学历、信用分、周一早上九点。它们是发明还是发现？承认能被撤回，是否意味着它们比石头更脆弱、还是反而更结实（石头砸不动一条法律）？普通人能改动其中哪一层，又在哪一层撞上真正的铁？可带进涂尔干的社会事实、霍布斯与卢梭的立约、韦伯的正当性、哈拉瑞的共同虚构，对上唯物论者。　也含：一个想法怎么从『离经叛道』变成『天经地义』——零、负数、虚数都曾被斥为荒谬、抵制数百年才成正典；有偿献血、人寿保险也曾被视为亵渎。可带进库恩的范式转移、福柯的知识型、拉图尔与玛丽·道格拉斯，对上实在论；并追问我们笃信的『客观』有多少靠审稿、复核这类把关共同体在替我们担保。
candidates.note_en: They grow neither in atoms nor in any single person's head: they persist because many people recognise them together, and would genuinely vanish if everyone stopped at once, a banknote reverting to paper. This 'jointly built' reality is neither material nor mental, yet it governs ordinary lives more than almost anything — house prices, credentials, credit scores, nine o'clock on Monday. Are they invented or discovered? Does the fact that recognition can be withdrawn make them more fragile than a stone, or sturdier (no stone ever moved a statute)? Which layer can an ordinary person actually shift, and where do they hit genuine iron? Durkheim's social facts, the covenants of Hobbes and Rousseau, Weber on legitimacy and Harari's shared fictions, set against the materialists. Also: how an idea travels from heresy to common sense — zero, negative and imaginary numbers were each denounced as absurd and resisted for centuries before entering the canon, and paid blood donation and life insurance were once treated as desecration. Kuhn's paradigm shifts, Foucault's épistémè, Latour and Mary Douglas can be brought against realism here; and it is worth asking how much of what we call objective is in fact underwritten for us by gatekeeping communities — referees, replicators, people who agree to stand behind a claim.

candidates.q: 一件事被解释清楚，就变得不值钱了吗？
candidates.q_en: Does explaining something drain the value out of it?
candidates.note: 告诉一个人他的爱情是催产素、他的敬畏是颞叶放电、他的直觉是贝叶斯更新，很多人立刻觉得被贬低了；可没有人在知道彩虹是折射之后就不再看彩虹。这种『一被解释就掉价』的感觉从哪里来——它只是一种心理错觉，还是在提醒我们某样东西确实被拿走了？济慈抱怨牛顿拆散了彩虹，费曼说懂得花的结构只会让它更美，韦伯把这一整个过程叫作祛魅。也含一层实用的：把动机、习惯、亲密关系拆成机制之后，人还剩下多少行动的力气；什么时候该看机制，什么时候该把说明书放下。
candidates.note_en: Tell someone their love is oxytocin, their awe is temporal-lobe activity, their intuition Bayesian updating, and many feel demoted on the spot — yet nobody stopped looking at rainbows on learning about refraction. Where does this devaluation-by-explanation come from: is it merely a psychological illusion, or a signal that something really has been taken away? Keats complained that Newton unwove the rainbow, Feynman held that knowing a flower's structure only adds to its beauty, and Weber named the whole process disenchantment. There is a practical layer too: once motives, habits and intimacy have been decomposed into mechanisms, how much force to act is left, and when should one look at the mechanism and when put the manual down?

candidates.q: 你的工作是真被需要，还是被造出来的？
candidates.q_en: Is your job actually needed, or was it invented?
candidates.note: 会照开、表照填、人人被需要，却没有一件事会因为你缺席而不成立。组织能不能批量制造出仪式性的岗位来维持活力？一个人怎么分辨自己每天做的事是被真实需要，还是被造出来让他有事做——而如果分辨出来了，又该拿这个答案怎么办。当岗位被切至极碎——分拣、审核、按脚本回话——"事上磨练"里那件值得磨的"事"本身也变小了：这条工夫论是否只对幸运的岗位成立？
candidates.note_en: The meetings still held, the forms still filed, everyone needed — and nothing that would fail to happen in your absence. Can an organization manufacture ceremonial posts wholesale in order to keep itself busy? How does a person tell whether what they do each day is genuinely required or produced so they have something to do — and what should they do with the answer once they have it?. And when a role is sliced down to the finest grain — sorting, moderating, reading from a script — the "affair worth tempering" in classical work-discipline is itself shrunk: does that discipline still hold outside of the fortunate jobs?

candidates.q: 文凭和执照，到底在保护谁？
candidates.q_en: Diplomas and licences: whom do they actually protect?
candidates.note: 医生、律师、教师、电工都要持牌，理由是保护外行免于庸手；可同一道门也把想进来的人挡在外面，并替在里面的人维持稀缺。一张证书证明的究竟是能力，还是排过队的资格？当能力越来越能被按次租用、一个没有任何文凭的人可以持续把事做对，什么样的社会安排才会承认他——作品集、公开的实绩、还是必须再考一次？也含一条更硬的分支：取消准入会不会先伤到最没有议价能力的人。可带进伊里奇的去学校化与专业垄断、斯密对行会的抨击、韦伯的科层与文凭制、以及行医与建筑执照的真实事故史。
candidates.note_en: Doctors, lawyers, teachers and electricians all need a licence, on the ground that laymen must be protected from incompetents; yet the same door keeps out those who want in and preserves scarcity for those already inside. Does a certificate attest to capability, or to having stood in the right queue? As competence becomes rentable by the call and someone with no diploma can get the work right again and again, what arrangement would ever let that count — a portfolio, a public track record, or one more examination? A harder branch follows: would abolishing entry requirements hurt first the people with the least bargaining power? Illich on deschooling and professional monopoly, Smith's attack on the guilds, Weber on bureaucracy and credentialism, and the real accident history behind medical and building licences all belong here.

candidates.q: 监控为什么总是朝下查？
candidates.q_en: Why does scrutiny always run downhill?
candidates.note: 被查的几乎总是位置更低的那一方：员工被背调、被绩效监控、被试用期，老板不被；保姆工作的家里装着摄像头，雇主家里没有；孩子的手机被翻，父母的不被。若『该不该核查』在实践中等于『上位者该不该用这项特权』，那么正当性是不是该用一条对等性判据来判——这项核查能不能反过来施加给提出它的人？还有一层现实的推力：当协作被拆到远程、外包、跨时区，一起挨骂、一起熬夜这些共同暴露的机会先没了，组织于是改用监控去补那个缺口——补得上吗，还是只是把成本换了个地方付？边沁的全景敞视、福柯的规训、法家的『察必有法』与信任的生理基础在此相撞。　另一面是举证责任的换肩：从前说一句『我有录音』就够了，如今得先证明录音不是合成的，而这份新增成本压在最没有资源的人身上——被欠薪的、被家暴的、遭遇医疗事故的。哪些事该在发生的当下就留证？制度该不该把自证责任还回去，让机构而非个人承担记录义务？
candidates.note_en: The person checked is almost always the one lower down: employees get background checks, performance monitoring and probation periods while their bosses do not; there is a camera in the house where the nanny works and none in the employer's; the child's phone is searched and the parent's is not. If 'should there be verification' amounts in practice to 'should those above use this privilege', should legitimacy be settled by a reciprocity test — can this piece of scrutiny be turned around on whoever proposed it? There is also a structural push behind it: once work is broken into remote, outsourced, cross-time-zone pieces, the occasions for shared exposure disappear first and organisations reach for surveillance to plug the gap. Does it plug, or does it merely move where the cost is paid? Bentham's panopticon, Foucault on discipline, the Legalist demand that inspection follow public statute, and the physiology of trust all collide here. The other face of this is the shifting of the burden of proof: saying 'I have a recording' used to be enough, and now the recording itself must be shown not to be synthetic — a new cost that falls on those with the fewest resources, the unpaid worker, the battered partner, the victim of a medical error. What should be documented the moment it happens? And should the duty of record-keeping be handed back to institutions rather than left with individuals?

candidates.q: 谁还愿意对你说真话？
candidates.q_en: Who is still willing to tell you the truth?
candidates.note: 顺着你说的东西越来越多：讨好带来留存，顶撞带来卸载；职位越高，听到的坏消息越少；朋友怕伤感情，医生怕纠纷，下属怕报复。于是判断一个信息源是否可信，最锋利的一条也许不是它对不对，而是它敢不敢说你不想听的话。这种『愿意得罪你』的能力该怎么保住——靠制度设计、靠挑人，还是靠自己先变得听得进去？谁又有动机去造一个会反驳你的东西？　同一道题还有一个对内的版本：受害者与加害者对同一件事记的是两本账，中间差着一个数量级——一方记得起因久远、伤害持续，另一方记得事出有因、早已翻篇。既然每个人都当过两种角色，你怎么可能知道自己不是正在低估？有没有外部装置——第三方复述、书面对账、一组固定的提问——能让人看见自己账本上被压掉的那一栏？
candidates.note_en: More and more of what surrounds us agrees with us: agreement drives retention and contradiction drives uninstalls; the higher the post, the less bad news reaches it; friends fear hurting you, doctors fear disputes, subordinates fear reprisal. So the sharpest test of a source may not be whether it is right but whether it dares say what you would rather not hear. How is that willingness to offend you preserved — by institutional design, by choosing the right people, or by first becoming someone who can take it? And who has any incentive to build something that contradicts you? The same question has an inward version: victim and perpetrator keep two different ledgers on one event, and the gap runs to an order of magnitude — one remembers a cause reaching far back and harm still continuing, the other a provocation and a matter long closed. Since everyone has occupied both roles, how could you know you are not the one underestimating? Is there an external device — a third party's retelling, a written reconciliation of accounts, a fixed set of questions — that shows a person the column they have compressed?

candidates.q: 现在的我，能替将来的我做主吗？
candidates.q_en: Can the person you are now decide for the person you will be?
candidates.note: 预嘱、婚约、戒断合约、把手机锁进定时盒——我们不断替一个还没到场的自己签字，而那个人未必同意。最尖锐的一处在临终：十年前写下的意愿，与今天那个不记得自己签过字、看上去也并不痛苦的人，该听谁的？往回推，同一道题也管着戒瘾、储蓄与婚姻：把未来的自己当作需要被约束的对象，是自律，还是对一个尚未到场者的专断？奥德修斯把自己绑上桅杆是明智的，可他至少还是同一个人；而人格、偏好与价值观本来就会漂移，若承认这一点，一纸事先的承诺凭什么压过此刻活着的那个人？
candidates.note_en: Advance directives, marriage vows, sobriety contracts, a phone locked in a timer box — we are forever signing on behalf of a self who has not yet arrived and may not agree. The sharpest case is at the end of life: a wish written ten years ago versus the person today who does not remember signing it and appears untroubled — whose word governs? Wound back, the same question runs through addiction, saving and marriage: is treating your future self as something to be bound self-discipline, or high-handedness toward someone not in the room? Odysseus was wise to be lashed to the mast, but he at least remained the same man; personality, preferences and values drift, and if we admit that, on what grounds does a prior promise outrank the person who is alive right now?

candidates.q: 专业人士能因信念拒绝服务吗？
candidates.q_en: May a professional refuse to serve on grounds of conscience?
candidates.note: 医生拒绝执行、药剂师拒绝配药、公务员拒绝登记、面包师拒绝接单——同一条『良心自由』用在不同的人身上，多数人的直觉常常相反。若允许拒绝，被立为权利的服务在缺人手的地方就形同虚设，越偏远越无人可去；若不许拒绝，成本会一路摊派到最难说不的那一层人身上，最终由资历最浅的人执行。判据该是什么：这份职业有没有垄断地位、当地有没有替代者、拒绝的是某个行为还是某类人？而一份需要良心才做得好的工作，能不能同时要求从业者把良心留在门外？
candidates.note_en: A doctor declining to perform, a pharmacist declining to dispense, a registrar declining to register, a baker declining an order — the same freedom of conscience, applied to different people, pulls most intuitions in opposite directions. Permit refusal and a service established as a right becomes hollow wherever staffing is thin, with the remote areas emptiest of all; forbid it and the cost slides down to the people least able to say no, until the most junior hands are the ones doing it. What should the criteria be — whether the profession holds a monopoly, whether a local alternative exists, whether what is refused is an act or a class of person? And can work that is only done well by people with a conscience also demand that they leave it at the door?

candidates.q: 旅行者来了之后，当地人得到了什么？
candidates.q_en: When the travellers arrive, what do the locals get?
candidates.note: 民宿把长租房源抽走、老街按游客的口味重做一遍、旺季挤到本地人自己出不了门——旅游带来的收入与代价从来不落在同一批人身上。一边是它确实养活了整条街的生计、也是许多地方唯一的外部收入；一边是房租、水源、公共空间被一种可以随时离开的需求重新定价。旅行者有没有义务了解自己的重量？该由谁来定这个限度——市场、当地政府，还是住在那里的人？同一把尺也量得到数字游民与短租平台。
candidates.note_en: Short-let listings drain the long-term rental stock, old streets are remade to a visitor's taste, and in peak season residents cannot get through their own town — the income tourism brings and the costs it imposes never land on the same people. On one side it genuinely feeds a whole street and is the only outside income many places have; on the other, rents, water and public space get repriced by a demand that can leave at any moment. Do travellers owe it to a place to understand their own weight? And who should set the limit — the market, the local authority, or the people who live there? The same ruler reaches digital nomads and short-let platforms.

candidates.q: 观念是怎么从异端变成常识的？
candidates.q_en: How does a heresy turn into common sense?
candidates.note: 举证责任在主张者、婚姻要双方同意、儿童不该做工——今天几乎不必再论证的判断，多半在几代人以前还是少数人的激进主张。论证在一个人身上很少奏效，却能在两三代之后变成默认：它先进教材，再进法律，最后进语感。这条传导链究竟怎么运作，中间漫长的成本由谁承担、谁最先付？反过来问同样锋利：今天被当成常识、其实从没被检验过的判断有哪些，又该怎么把它们找出来？
candidates.note_en: That the burden of proof lies with whoever asserts, that a marriage requires both parties' consent, that children should not work — judgements now barely in need of defence were, a few generations back, the radical claims of a minority. An argument seldom moves the person in front of you, yet two or three generations later it has become the default: into textbooks first, then law, finally the ear. How does that transmission actually work, who carries the long cost in between, and who pays first? The question cuts as sharply in reverse: which of today's unexamined common sense has never been tested, and how would you find it?

debated.q: 是地理塑造了思想，还是思想自有其命？
debated.q_en: Did geography shape thought, or do ideas have a life of their own?

debated.q: 想活得不后悔，该入世还是出世？
debated.q_en: To live without regret: engage the world, or withdraw from it?

debated.q: 为什么我们忍不住跟别人比？嫉妒能消除吗？
debated.q_en: Why can't we stop comparing ourselves to others — and can envy ever be cured?

debated.q: 如果有了足够的钱（财务自由），是否还应该继续工作？
debated.q_en: If you had enough money to never need to, should you still work?

debated.q: 量子物理是否说明「观测」真的改变了世界？
debated.q_en: Does quantum physics show that 'observation' really changes the world?

debated.q: AI 时代，人的心智该往「深」练还是往「广」练？——不受打扰的深度专注，还是驾驭多线程的调度与切换？
debated.q_en: In the AI era, should the mind train for depth or breadth — undistracted deep focus, or orchestrating and switching across many threads?

debated.q: 品德是教出来的，还是长出来的？——美德到底可不可教？
debated.q_en: Can virtue be taught — is character instilled, or does it grow on its own?

debated.q: 普通人该进大厂求稳，还是闯小公司、创业？
debated.q_en: Should you join a big company for stability, or take a startup — or strike out on your own?

debated.q: 贫富差距本身会让人生病吗？——该不该把不平等当成一个公共健康问题？
debated.q_en: Does the wealth gap itself make people sick — and should inequality be treated as a public-health problem?

debated.q: 教育到底是为了什么——筛选人才的机器，还是培养人的土壤？
debated.q_en: What is education actually for — a machine to sort talent, or soil to cultivate a person?

debated.q: AI 时代，该练流体智力还是晶体智力？
debated.q_en: In the age of AI: train fluid intelligence, or crystallized?

debated.q: 数学是被发现的，还是被发明的？
debated.q_en: Is mathematics discovered, or invented?

debated.q: 进步是真的吗？历史是在前进，还是循环、甚至退步？
debated.q_en: Is progress real? Is history moving forward, in cycles — or even backward?

debated.q: 现代的『文明进步』，是解放还是控制？
debated.q_en: Modern 'civilizational progress': liberation, or control?

debated.q: 容颜该顺其自然地老去，还是该努力医美、抗衰？
debated.q_en: Should we let our looks age naturally, or fight it with cosmetic work and anti-aging?

debated.q: AI 有没有、或可能有意识？我们又凭什么判断？
debated.q_en: Does (or could) AI have consciousness — and how would we ever know?

debated.q: 语言塑造思维吗？说不同语言的人，看到的是不同的世界吗？
debated.q_en: Does language shape thought? Do speakers of different languages see different worlds?

debated.q: 美，是主观感受，还是有客观的标准？
debated.q_en: Is beauty just in the eye of the beholder, or is there an objective standard?

debated.q: 我们为何系统性地低估『照护与情感劳动』的价值？（带孩子、陪伴、安抚、协调——这些撑起一切却没人记功的活）
debated.q_en: Why do we systematically undervalue care and emotional labor?

debated.q: 绩效考核与「赛马」（KPI、末位淘汰）是激励，还是毒药？
debated.q_en: Are performance metrics and forced ranking (KPIs, stack-ranking) a motivator, or a poison?

debated.q: 我们对远方陌生人的苦难，负有多大义务？
debated.q_en: How much do we owe the suffering of distant strangers?

debated.q: 拖延症，到底要不要治？
debated.q_en: Should we cure procrastination at all?

debated.q: 全球化正在让世界失去文化多样性吗？
debated.q_en: Is globalization costing us cultural diversity?

debated.q: 真爱是发现的，还是培养（甚至建构）出来的？
debated.q_en: Is true love found, or cultivated — even constructed?

debated.q: 公司到底该对谁负责——只对股东，还是也对员工与社会？
debated.q_en: Whom does a company answer to — only shareholders, or also its workers and society?

debated.q: 人真的在逃避自由吗？——自由是解放，还是一副人宁愿卸下的重担？
debated.q_en: Do humans really flee from freedom — is freedom liberation, or a burden people would rather set down?

debated.q: 该主动过「极简 / 少欲」的生活吗？
debated.q_en: Should we deliberately live simply?

debated.q: 「社会兴趣」是衡量活得好不好的尺吗？
debated.q_en: Is 'social interest' the yardstick of a life well lived?

debated.q: 濒死体验证明意识能脱离大脑吗？
debated.q_en: Do near-death experiences prove consciousness can leave the brain?

debated.q: 时间真的存在吗，还是一种幻觉？
debated.q_en: Does time really exist, or is it an illusion?

debated.q: 我们对地球（其他物种、后代）负有怎样的义务？
debated.q_en: What do we owe the Earth — other species, and future generations?

debated.q: 我们是不是正在失去『第三空间』？
debated.q_en: Are we losing our 'third places'?

debated.q: 该不该让算法来管人——派活、打分、监控，甚至解雇？
debated.q_en: Should algorithms manage people — assigning work, scoring, surveilling, even firing?

debated.q: 维系和谐，有时是否比说出真相更重要？（含：伪善是不是比赤裸的恶更可恨——道德表演与『人设』，究竟是文明的润滑剂还是腐蚀剂）
debated.q_en: Is keeping the peace sometimes more important than telling the truth? (Including: is hypocrisy more contemptible than open vice — is moral performance the lubricant of civilisation or its solvent?)

debated.q: 宇宙真的是「黑暗森林」吗？文明之间注定你死我活，还是可能合作？
debated.q_en: Is the universe really a 'dark forest'? Are civilizations doomed to mutual annihilation, or can they cooperate?

debated.q: 该不该用 AI「复活」逝去的亲人？
debated.q_en: Should you use AI to 'resurrect' a dead loved one?

debated.q: 自由与平等不可兼得时，该牺牲哪个？
debated.q_en: When liberty and equality cannot both be had, which gives way?

debated.q: 当 AI 比谁都懂，领导者还剩什么不可替代的？（含：最稀缺的会不会是『会读人』——读懂人、拿捏分寸、在冲突里维系信任的社会情感能力，机器能不能接管）
debated.q_en: When AI knows more than anyone, what is left that only a leader can do? (Including: will the scarcest skill turn out to be reading people — judging a face, calibrating tone, holding trust together through conflict — and can machines take that over?)

debated.q: 爱一个人，该介入他的人生多深？
debated.q_en: How far should love intervene in another's life?

debated.q: 该为过去的选择后悔吗？
debated.q_en: Should we regret the choices we made?

debated.q: 真的存在平行宇宙吗？
debated.q_en: Do parallel universes really exist?

debated.q: 有什么是金钱不该买卖的？
debated.q_en: Is there anything money should not be able to buy?

debated.q: 职场该不该表达野心？
debated.q_en: Should you show your ambition at work?

debated.q: 园丁还是木匠？——父母该「雕琢」孩子，还是营造环境让他自己长成？
debated.q_en: Gardener or carpenter — should parents shape the child, or cultivate the soil and let them grow unpredictably?

debated.q: 真正的『勇气』是什么？
debated.q_en: What is courage, really?

debated.q: 世界是唯物的，还是唯心的？
debated.q_en: Is the world made of matter, or of mind?

debated.q: 物质极度丰裕后，人会走向衰亡吗？
debated.q_en: Does material abundance lead to decline?

debated.q: AI 做完入门的活，新人怎么学本事？
debated.q_en: If AI does the entry-level work, how do novices learn?

debated.q: 忠诚该不该被考验？
debated.q_en: Should loyalty be tested — and is a trust that holds only while unverified really trust at all?

debated.q: 钱该省下来滚复利，还是该花掉？
debated.q_en: Should money be saved to compound, or spent?

debated.q: AI 能伪造一切，我们还信什么？
debated.q_en: When AI can fake anything, what is left to trust?

debated.q: 社会该不该允许安乐死与协助死亡？
debated.q_en: Should society allow euthanasia and assisted dying?

debated.q: 只有一条晋升阶梯的组织，浪费了谁？
debated.q_en: Who is wasted by an organisation with only one ladder?

debated.q: 趁年轻，该搏事业还是先去看世界？
debated.q_en: When young: build a career, or go see the world first?

debated.q: 该不该原谅伤害过你的人？
debated.q_en: Should you forgive someone who has wronged you?

debated.q: 理性与信仰冲突时，该让哪一个让步？
debated.q_en: When reason and faith collide, which should yield?
